html:
On 14 October 1973 hundreds of thousands of students and citizens in Bangkok forced the military dictator Thanom Kittikachorn out of the country. About 77 people were killed when troops fired on the crowds.

King Bhumibol stepped in to end the violence, which raised the monarchy's standing. Three years of open politics followed, with elections, strikes and peasant unions.

On 6 October 1976 police and right-wing militias attacked students at Thammasat University, killing dozens, and the army took power again. Many students fled to the communist guerrillas in the jungle, in the years of the Cold War. Both dates are still marked by Thai democrats. See 1932 revolution.
sum: On 14 October 1973 hundreds of thousands of students and citizens in Bangkok forced the military dictator Thanom Kittikachorn out of the country. About 77 people were killed when troops fired on the crowds.
